title: Your Contact Center Is About to Get Way More Expensive (Here's Why)
excerpt: AI adoption in customer service is skyrocketing, and the platforms you're comparing are pricing themselves differently — you need to understand the real math before you switch.

content.text: So I've been looking at what's happening in the contact center space right now, and there's this thing nobody's really talking about openly: the cost of adding AI to your customer service operation is all over the map depending on who you go with. And that matters a lot more than you'd think.

Here's what's going on. Contact center software used to be pretty straightforward — you paid per user, maybe a little extra for some features, done. But now that AI is basically table stakes (everyone's expected to have it), vendors are pricing it completely differently. Some are bundling it in. Some are charging extra per interaction. Some are doing per-user add-ons. And honestly, it's making it almost impossible to compare apples to apples.

Over 95% of field service and customer support organizations are now using AI tools. The question isn't whether to adopt it anymore — it's whether you can afford the way your platform is going to charge you for it.
Why This Matters to Your Bottom Line

Let's say you're running a small business with 10 customer service reps. You're looking at platforms that all seem comparable on the surface. One charges $50 per user per month. Another charges $35 but then tacks on $0.50 per AI-handled interaction. A third goes $60 but includes everything. The math can swing hundreds of dollars a month depending on your actual call volume and how much automation you end up using. And that's before you factor in setup, training, and integrations.

items: Different pricing models mean you can't just compare base prices anymore
Hidden costs sneak in through per-interaction fees, add-ons, and integration charges
More AI features don't automatically mean better ROI — depends entirely on your use case
Setup and training costs are often quoted separately but they stack up fast

content.text: What You Actually Need to Do

content.label: Intecha's Take
content.text: Before you talk to any vendor, map out your actual usage: How many calls/chats per month? How many agents do you really need software for? What specific things would AI actually handle for you (voicemails, simple questions, scheduling)? Then ask every platform the same three questions: What's the real monthly cost for *my* setup? What happens if we use more AI than we think? And what's not included in that price? Don't let them dodge the third one. Write down their answers. Compare the total cost, not the per-seat cost.

The truth is, the best contact center platform for you isn't the one with the flashiest AI or the lowest advertised price. It's the one where you understand exactly what you're paying for, where that cost aligns with how you actually work, and where you're not going to get surprised by fees six months in. Take the time to get that math right up front. It's worth it.
